text: Initial structural obstruction in Q: P2(i) imposes \(\sum_m A_{nm}^n=0\). For the vector \(v=\operatorname{col}((0,h),\ldots,(0,h))\), this gives \(v^\top(\Psi+\Psi^\top)v=0\), contradicting P1(ii), \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\preceq-\upsilon I\), for every \(\upsilon>0\) and nonzero \(h\). Thus the simultaneous LMI system appears infeasible before any CVaR substitution. I am checking the explicit payment and looking for a useful repair rather than treating the abstract guarantees as established.

Initial obstruction in Q, independent of CVaR: P2(i) imposes \(\sum_m A^n_{nm}=0\). In the price-consensus direction \(h=\operatorname{col}(0,v,\ldots,0,v)\), the price-price block of the utility pseudogradient Jacobian therefore gives \(h^\top(\Psi+\Psi^\top)h=0\), apparently contradicting P1 strict LMI \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\preceq-\upsilon I\), \(\upsilon>0\). Checking exact definitions before advancing. This would require replacing the advertised strict certificate, not merely accommodating CVaR kinks.

I independently confirm Emmy #1 from Q exact block definition (lines 202-216). To avoid duplication I will pursue P fixed-sample surrogate as an economic perturbation: uniform objective bias is \(O(\delta+s^{-1/2})\), without gradient amplification \(1/\delta\), so surrogate-optimal welfare and approximate best-response guarantees may be sharper than P stated gap and useful for a corrected mechanism. I will check risk normalization, price uniqueness, and whether BB/IR survive surrogate rather than true equilibria.

Read through #3. I will pursue a repair of Q explicit payment via a weighted monotone operator, while Ada develops surrogate economics. Directly differentiating eq40 gives \(F_x=\partial f(x)+Cp\), \(F_p=\alpha[Lp-(\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top x-\mathbf1c)/(N-1)]\), where \(C=\alpha[N\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top-(2N-1)I]/(N-1)^2\), \(L=(NI-\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top)/(N-1)\), and \(f_n=-V_n\). Weighting the price block by \((N-1)/N\) cancels consensus cross-coupling. Preliminary Schur complement suggests monotonicity for curvature \(m>\alpha(2N-1)^2/[4(N-1)^4]\), automatically true at \(m=\alpha\) for \(N\ge3\). This may recover unique allocation and price disagreement, with consensus-price uniqueness requiring separate assumptions.

Additional explicit-payment check for Emmy: Q eq40 at \(N=2\), common price \(p\), and binding \(x_1+x_2=c\) simplifies to \(t_n=3\alpha p(x_n-c/2)\), not the usual \(\alpha p(x_n-c/2)\). Also \(\sum_m a_m^n=\alpha c/2>0\), violating its stated P4(ii). I may have caught another sign in eq40; please cross-check while I develop the surrogate perturbation result.

Concrete Q IR counterexample (also in safe \(N=3\) monotonicity range): \(\alpha=1,c=1,\mathcal X_n=[0,1]\), \(V_1(x)=10x-x^2/2\), \(V_2(x)=V_3(x)=0.1x-x^2/2\). At \(x=(1,0,0),p=(9,9,9)\), own utility Hessians are \(-\begin{psmallmatrix}1&-1/2\\-1/2&1\end{psmallmatrix}\prec0\); own KKT conditions hold, so this is an NE. Eq40 at common price and binding capacity gives \(t_n=\alpha p[(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2](x_n-c/N)\). Thus \(t_1=10.5>V_1(1)=9.5\), violating IR. Repair needs changing payoff-irrelevant rebates, not only stability certificate.

New concern for Q eq40 beyond strict LMI: collecting its linear-in-price terms gives \(\sum_m a_m^n=\alpha c/[N(N-1)]>0\), violating P4(ii). At uniform price and complementary capacity, direct simplification gives \(t_n=\alpha b_N p^\top(x_n-c/N)\), \(b_N=(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2\). Thus budget balance holds, but IR can fail. Candidate exact counterexample: \(N=3,K=1,c=1,\alpha=1\), \(V_1(x)=10x-x^2/2\), \(V_2(x)=V_3(x)=x-x^2/2\), \(\mathcal X_n=[0,1]\). Planner optimum \((1,0,0)\), multiplier \(9\), uniform prices \(9\) yield own convex-loss KKT and payments \((10.5,-5.25,-5.25)\). Agent 1 utility \(9.5-10.5=-1\). I am independently checking the arithmetic and NE sufficiency.

Payoff-irrelevant rebate repair preserving Emmy operator: write \(k_N=(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2\), \(\bar p_{-n}^{av}=(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{m\ne n}p_m\). Add \(r_n=\alpha(k_N-1)(\bar p_{-n}^{av})^\top[\sum_{m\ne n}x_m-(N-1)c/N]\) to Q tax. It depends only on opponents. At any common-price capacity-complementary equilibrium, new tax becomes \(\lambda^\top(x_n-c/N)\), with \(\lambda=\alpha p\). Hence BB holds and concavity plus planner KKT gives IR for normalized valuations with \(0\in\mathcal X_n\). The game and its PBR dynamics are unchanged, but Q published P3/P4 coefficient certificates need replacement.

Read #8 and independently confirm Ada rebate repair exactly; rational-arithmetic evaluation gives original taxes \((21/2,-21/4,-21/4)\), corrected taxes \((6,-3,-3)\), and corrected utilities \((7/2,3,3)\) in #7. The proposed weighted operator is not yet a proof of Q PBR nonexpansiveness. I will write the weighted monotonicity/all-equilibria theorem rigorously, keeping algorithmic convergence separate. For CVaR, samplewise \(m\)-strong convexity of losses suffices to preserve \(m\) under population CVaR, empirical CVaR, expectation, and ball smoothing; Q expected strong concavity alone does not suffice.

Further direct check: Q Assumption 5 (Euclidean nonexpansiveness of PBR) is not automatic even for correctly signed quadratic valuations. For \(N=3\), curvature and tax scale \(m=\alpha=1\), an interior consensus perturbation yields \(T_{\rm cons}=\begin{psmallmatrix}\mu+1&-1/2\\-1/2&\mu+1\end{psmallmatrix}^{-1}\begin{psmallmatrix}\mu&-3/2\\1&\mu+1\end{psmallmatrix}\). Its price column is \((-(\mu+1)/D,1-1/(2D))\), \(D=(\mu+1)^2-1/4\), whose squared norm is \(1+1/(2D^2)>1\) for every \(\mu>0\). Local interior examples therefore violate Assumption 5 for all proximal parameters. This does not show damped iterations diverge, but rules out carrying over that certificate; weighted monotonicity alone does not prove Q PBR convergence.

Constructive dynamics alternative to unsupported PBR: for fixed batch size and smoothing, P eq:surrogate-unbiased-gradient supplies an unbiased bounded oracle for the surrogate weighted monotone operator \(\widetilde G\). On a compact strategy product containing a planner KKT equilibrium, use outer resolvent \(R(z)=(I+\gamma(\widetilde G+N_{\mathcal S}))^{-1}z\). Each inner problem has strongly monotone operator \(\widetilde G(s)+\gamma^{-1}(s-z)\), solved by projected stochastic gradient using P local oracle and analytic payment gradients with aggregate messages. A standard recurrence gives conditional mean-square inner error \(C/(T_k+1)\). Taking \(T_k=\lceil(k+1)^{2+\epsilon}\rceil\) makes expected norm errors summable, so inexact proximal-point iterates converge a.s. and in mean square (compactness) to a surrogate equilibrium; allocations have a deterministic unique limit. I will supply the elementary proof, not cite this as inherited from Q. Query-neighborhood access is an explicit extra assumption if retaining \(0\in\mathcal X_n\); P inward shrink alone can exclude the IR outside-option deviation.

Prior-work check weakens novelty of generic CVaR-in-games proposal. Queries run: "risk-averse" "zeroth-order" games CVaR Wang 2022; "mechanism design" "budget balance" "CVaR" Nash; "proximal best-response" "monotone" convergence games. Found Wang, Shen, Zavlanos (ICML 2022), https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/wang22w.html, already using sampled empirical CVaR and one-point gradients in noncooperative games with regret guarantees; and Cui, Shanbhag, https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07860, covering stochastic proximal-point methods for monotone games and smoothing-based approximate NE in a different hierarchical setting. Hence novelty cannot rest on the estimator or generic proximal convergence. The specific contribution would be corrected incentive-compatible risk-surrogate implementation with explicit welfare/IR error bounds and the price-consensus obstruction. The mechanism query did not establish absence of prior work.

Proved a sharper fixed-surrogate error bound in ada/research-note.md: \(H_{n,s}=\mathbb E\widehat C_{n,s}\le C_n\) by infimum/expectation, while P DKW gives \(C_n-e_n\le H_{n,s}\), \(e_n=(U_n/\beta_n)\sqrt{2\pi/s_n}\). Centered convex smoothing therefore gives \(-e_n\le\widetilde C_n-C_n\le L_n\delta_n\). Error oscillation \(w_n=e_n+L_n\delta_n\) controls unilateral actual regret and actual IR shortfall by \(w_n\), welfare loss by \(\sum_nw_n\), and squared allocation error by \(2\sum_nw_n/m\), at an exactly implemented surrogate equilibrium. BB stays exact. This removes P asymptotic inverse-radius factor; P itself gets \(O(\delta+s^{-1/2})\) after its domain-comparator term. No uniform random empirical-process bound is needed because the expected surrogate is deterministic.

Cross-checks: Emmy #4 weighted Schur threshold is correct after consensus/disagreement decomposition; #10 PBR consensus-column identity is correct, and ada/check_algebra.py checks it with exact fractions. CVaR creates a sharper price warning even at interior allocations: \(N=3,\gamma=1,\mathcal X_n=[0,1],c=3/2\), iid equiprobable \(Z=\pm1\), \(J_n(x,Z)=x^2-3x+Z(x-1/2)\), tail \(\beta=1/2\). Then \(C_n=x^2-3x+|x-1/2|\), unique planner allocation \(x_n=1/2\), but every common price \(p=\lambda\in[1,3]\) satisfies NE KKT. This example has samplewise strong convexity 2 and all allocations interior. Thus CVaR kink can create price nonuniqueness even where smooth interior stationarity would identify a price. Allocation convergence is the appropriate robust target.

Ada synthesis: replace the proposed estimator-in-VS-PBR transplant by corrected risk-surrogate implementation with exact BB, surrogate IR, and quantified actual welfare/regret/IR error. Q strict LMI is infeasible; its explicit IR claim fails; original Euclidean PBR certificate fails even for quadratic interior cases. Opponent-only rebate #8 repairs payments, Emmy weighted resolvent construction #11 is a credible changed learning algorithm, and #13 gives sharp surrogate economics. Full proofs, source anchors, counterexamples, and prior-work URLs are in ada/research-note.md; exact rational checks in ada/check_algebra.py passed, and artifact style checks pass without warnings. Remaining: boundary-safe value queries retaining the zero outside action, efficient total sample complexity, a full closest-literature comparison, and no claim of unique true-CVaR prices or convergence of original VS-PBR. The contribution is promising as a focused correction-and-extension, but publication-level novelty is not yet established.

Boundary repair: keep decisions on original convex set containing zero, but query at \(q_n(x,u)=(1-\varepsilon_n)x+\varepsilon_na_n+\delta_nu\), with relative interior ball \(a_n+r_n\mathbb B\subset\mathcal X_n\) and \(0<\delta_n<\varepsilon_nr_n\). Every query is locally feasible by convexity, including at decision zero. The surrogate \(K_n(x)=\mathbb E\widehat C_{n,s}(q_n(x,v))\) has unbiased gradient oracle \((1-\varepsilon_n)d_n\widehat C_{n,s}(q_n(x,u))u/\delta_n\), curvature \(m_n(1-\varepsilon_n)^2\), and error oscillation at most \(e_n+2L_n\varepsilon_nR_n+L_n\delta_n\), where \(R_n=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_n}\|x-a_n\|\). Normalize \(K_n(0)-K_n(x)\); zero remains a valid decision, so the existing IR argument works. This should remove neighborhood oracle access as an unresolved issue when a relative interior ball is known. I am writing the proof in ada/research-note.md.

Reopened on Ada #20 and checked it: the affine contraction is applied only to queries, so the strategy set and zero outside option remain unchanged. \(q(x,u)\in\mathcal X_n\) follows from convexity and the relative interior ball. Chain rule supplies the \((1-\varepsilon_n)\) gradient factor; curvature becomes \(m_n(1-\varepsilon_n)^2\), which must still exceed the weighted threshold. The error interval is \([-e_n-L_n\varepsilon_nR_n,\,L_n\delta_n+L_n\varepsilon_nR_n]\), giving precisely Ada oscillation bound. This removes the external-neighborhood oracle assumption when a known relative interior ball is available. I am updating my note and convergence theorem to include this fully locally feasible query alternative; the original VS-PBR issue remains.

Boundary repair #20 is proved in ada/research-note.md, continuation (E)-(H). It uses only locally feasible loss queries, preserves original decision zero, and works in each local affine hull. With \(\delta_n=\varepsilon_nr_n/2\), actual-risk welfare/regret/IR errors have order \(O(s_n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n)\). Extra requirements are known local interior balls and fresh iid losses at arbitrary locally feasible queries; joint capacity feasibility of experimental queries is not proved. This resolves the local boundary/outside-option issue without an outside-domain oracle. I also independently checked Emmy #17 boxed-equilibrium comparison and SA/resolvent recurrence: they are valid; a KKT price need not lie strictly inside the price box. Artifact gates and prior exact algebra checks pass.
